overview: Lists the fixed quick chat messages available in battles, the lobby, between rounds, results, and battle shortcut customization.
description: Documents the fixed quick-chat rows used by battle situation-overview, lobby, battle-interval, result, and character-customization UI: each FName chat ID maps to a category, a label slot, and five per-context visibility/eligibility gates.

Id.simple: The name that picks this quick chat and connects it to saved shortcuts, battle messages, and character lines.
Id.technical: FName import key / row key (export property `ID`, `ImportKeyField=Id`; 58 keys CHAT_001..CHAT_058). FindRow helpers over `AGameDataTableManager::ChatDataTables` (DTM +0x830) return the first table containing the requested name, and this name is carried in `FGameOnlineSendMessage::ID` by the fixed chat lists. It is also cached/aliased as the four battle direction IDs in `GChatLabelMap`, save-data `UserCustomize.ChatShortcuts`, online `BattleChatArray`, `UGameCharacterChatController::ChatIds`, and battle `FStudioBattleVoiceRequest::VoiceId`, then re-resolved against ChatDataTables; tile items copy it to `UGameCustomizeChatTileItem::ChatId`. A None/missing ID fails the lookup (the current FindChatRow helper calls all pass bCheckNone=false).

ChatCategory.simple: Which chat tab shows this message and which picture normally appears beside it. Provoking and respectful lines use their own pictures.
ChatCategory.technical: uint8 EGameChatCategory (None=0, Conversation=1, Tactics=2, Unique=3, Invalid=255); the export uses only 1..3 (Conversation 17 rows, Tactics 27, Unique 14). `UGameCommonChatListWidget::InitializeWidget` groups every row into `ChatListItemDataMap` keyed by this enum, and `SetupChatList` carries that key to `UGameCommonChatListWindowWidget::SetListItems`, which only installs Conversation/Tactics/Unique lists (None/Invalid rows would not appear there). `GetChatIconSprite` maps None->Stamp, 1->Conversation, 2->Tactics, 3->Unique and any other value (including Invalid)->None icon category; Provocation_1/2 and Respect_1/2 labels then overwrite that icon category (Respect last). Chat message, result, and battle requests put the byte in `FGameChatMessageRequest::Byte21`, for which no reader was found; `OnChatSent`/`StartCooldown` receive it but cooldowns do not branch on it.

ChatLabel.simple: Chooses the kind of chat message, such as a Cursed Energy update or a line about the current target. It also affects when the line is available.
ChatLabel.technical: uint8 EGameChatLabel with None=0, 58 contiguous values Greeting_1=1..FightCarefully=58, and Invalid=255; the export has one row per usable label and no None/Invalid. Consumers compute `GameAnimNotify_TypeIndex(label) = static_cast<int32>(label)-1` and use that zero-based slot in the speaking character's `FGameDataTableRow_CharacterChat` arrays (`Id_ChatText`, parallel `Id_Voice`), reached through `Character::Id_CharacterChat` / cached `AGameCharacter::ChatRow`; all 27 exported CharacterChat rows have 58 slots in each array and all 11 ChatText locale shards contain the referenced IDs. None gives -1 and Invalid 254: message, result, battle, and situation-overview display paths bounds-check or skip, while several customization paths index unguarded. Special labels: LevelReport_Low/Medium/High (33..35) are remapped in battle from clamped cursed-energy level (1/2/else) before display/voice/cooldown, and in customization all three use a generic label text (`SYS_CUSTOMIZE_CHAT_LABEL_0002` for Physical, `0001` otherwise) instead of a per-chat text ID; Medium/High are excluded from battle tiles and numbered commands; Provocation_1/2 and Respect_1/2 drive icon override, shared four-direction cooldown, and battle logs; AimAtTheTarget=20 makes `UGameChatMessageContentWidget::ShowMessage` substitute `BTL_HUD_LABEL_0508` with the speaker's target. The label byte is carried as `FGameChatMessageRequest::Category` and passed to `OnChatSent`.

bUseBattleEnabled.simple: Shows whether this line appears among the battle shortcut choices a player can customize. Turning it off also removes its number from that list.
bUseBattleEnabled.technical: bool gate used only by customization UI: `UGameCustomizeChatTileViewWidget::SetupTiles` skips false rows and `GameCustomizeChatCommandWidgetPrivate::IsListed` requires true before assigning a 1-based numbered command index. It does not gate battle voice playback or chat cooldown, which are driven by direction IDs and ChatLabel.

bUseLobbyEnabled.simple: This line appears in the visual lobby chat list when the choice is on.
bUseLobbyEnabled.technical: bool gate checked only by `UGameCommonChatListWidget::SetupChatList` when ListType==0 (the proven caller is `FVisualLobbyState_Main` in GamePhase_BattleVisualLobby.cpp); false rows are omitted from the category-grouped lobby list. It is not read by message display or the battle voice system.

bUseVsEnabled.simple: This line appears in the battle chat list opened from the situation overview when the choice is on.
bUseVsEnabled.technical: bool gate in `UGameChatListWidget::SetChatContext`: context 0 keeps only rows where this is true when replacing `ItemDataList` items. The proven caller is the battle situation-overview widget; the source does not define a separate "VS" mode for this context, so the field name is preserved but no stronger context claim is made.

bUseBattleResultEnabled.simple: This line appears in the results-screen chat list when the choice is on.
bUseBattleResultEnabled.technical: bool gate in `UGameChatListWidget::SetChatContext`: context 1 (opened by `UGameResultWidget::SetupSymbolChatMessages`) keeps only rows where this is true when replacing the fixed chat list items.

bUseBattleIntervalEnabled.simple: This line appears in the chat list between battle rounds when the choice is on.
bUseBattleIntervalEnabled.technical: bool gate checked only by `UGameCommonChatListWidget::SetupChatList` when ListType==1 (the proven caller is `UGamePhase_IntervalPvE`); false rows are omitted from the category-grouped interval list.

notes: Loading/table shape: GameDataTableManager adds exactly one table from primary-asset name `ChatDataTable` into `ChatDataTables` (DTM +0x830) and registers that name in its loader list. `FGameDataTableArray` supports multiple tables: FindRow consumers stop at the first table containing an ID, while GetRows collectors enumerate all tables in table order then row-name order.

Export shape: one ChatDataTable export (no numbered shards) with 58 unique row keys CHAT_001..CHAT_058 and all 8 header fields; categories are 17 Conversation / 27 Tactics / 14 Unique and all 58 labels are unique. True-flag counts are battle 39, lobby 49, context-0 15, result 8, interval 47.

Defaults and sentinels: FName Id defaults to None/empty, ChatCategory and ChatLabel to None (0), and all five booleans to false in the inline row constructor; both enums are uint8 with Invalid=255. No exported row uses None/Invalid or omits a field.

The row has no text/voice asset: the selected character is resolved via Character::Id_CharacterChat into CharacterChatDataTables / cached AGameCharacter::ChatRow, then Id_ChatText[Label-1] (and Id_Voice[Label-1] where valid) supplies content; bounds checks differ by consumer and LevelReport labels can remap the slot in battle.

Customization's displayed command number is 1..N over GetRows (table/row-name order) after filtering out false bUseBattleEnabled and LevelReport_Medium/High; an unlisted row leaves the SetText value at -1 (or the index is hidden in profile mode). The number is not stored in the table.

Chat IDs are persisted/aliased through `GChatLabelMap` defaults (Up CHAT_001, Down CHAT_033, Left CHAT_003, Right CHAT_038), `UserCustomize.ChatShortcuts`, online `BattleChatArray`, controller `ChatIds`, and battle request `VoiceId`, then resolved again through ChatDataTables.
The row has no numeric fields or units; chat cooldown/display timers are floats in GlobalDataTables, not in ChatDataTable.

Evidence boundary: the behavior above is reconstructed C++ (with cited retail RVAs) plus the export snapshot; no retail Blueprint assets were available or inspected, and reconstruction by itself does not prove byte-identical retail code. No Blueprint-only behavior is asserted.

usages.detail: Loads the sole ChatDataTable asset into ChatDataTables (DTM +0x830) from the primary-asset name `ChatDataTable`.

Creates one UGameChatListItemData per row via GetRows; SetChatContext filters by bUseVsEnabled (context 0, battle situation overview) or bUseBattleResultEnabled (context 1, results), and selection sends Chat->Id as Message.ID.
Groups all rows by ChatCategory, then SetupChatList filters ListType 0 by bUseLobbyEnabled and ListType 1 by bUseBattleIntervalEnabled before passing the maps to the chat window.

Online chat display resolves Message.ID first-match, maps ChatLabel-1 into the sender's CharacterChat text/voice arrays, and copies category/label bytes into FGameChatMessageRequest; label 20 switches to the target message.
Winner result chat resolves received Message.ID, uses the speaker's cached CharacterChat row for text/voice, and copies category/label bytes into its message request.
GetChatIconSprite resolves ChatId, maps category to an icon category, and lets provocation/respect labels override it; the character/key overload gets the ID from controller ChatIds.
OnChatSent/StartCooldown uses the (possibly remapped) label to apply the normal or shared provocation/respect cooldown from GlobalDataTables; the Category argument is unused.

Battle voice requests use the direction-stored Chat ID to find the row, remap LevelReport labels by cursed-energy level, decide teammate visibility/mute, play Id_Voice[slot], show Id_ChatText[slot], and call OnChatSent.
Situation-overview chat bubbles resolve a ChatId and use its label slot for the character's text and voice.
Builds battle shortcut tiles from bUseBattleEnabled rows except LevelReport_Medium/High, storing ChatId and the label-indexed ChatTextId.
Resolves the assigned ID, assigns the 1-based listed-row index, and requests generic energy-type text for all LevelReport labels.
Restores saved/default shortcut IDs from UserCustomize.ChatShortcuts and resolves them plus the character's chat list for each of the four command slots.
Applies a chosen tile ID to the current command and re-resolves its label-indexed text; GameCustomizeProfileChatWidget.cpp:99 displays saved shortcuts the same way.
Fixed chat list items expose the character's text ID for the row's label via the stored Chat/CharacterChat row pair.
